preamble: De-affrication of [ts] to [s] is a common historical development in which the stop onset of the affricate is lost, leaving only the sibilant fricative. It occurred in Old French (centum > [tsent] > [sɑ̃]), in 16th-century Spanish (where /ts/ deaffricated to [s̪] by 1600 before becoming Castilian /θ/ or merging with /s/ under seseo), and in prehistoric Greek, where *ts from palatalized *ky, *khy and *ty yielded Ionic ss (later simplified to [s] in Modern Greek). In southern Arawakan, Paunaka merged *ts with *s, and Terena deaffricated ts to s around the turn of the 20th century, as early Terena wordlists still show <ts>.

examples.note: Latin centum evolved into Old French [tsent], which subsequently de-affricated to [s] in Middle and Modern French.
By 1600 the affricate /ts/ (spelled c before e/i and ç) had deaffricated to dental [s̪]; in Andalusian, Canarian and American seseo it merged with /s/, so 'ciento' sounds like 'siento' 'I feel'.
Pre-Greek *ts arising from palatalization became Ionic σσ /sː/ (Attic ττ); similarly *tag-yō > *tatsō > τάσσω 'I arrange'. Modern Greek simplified the geminate to [s].
Proto-Muskogean is a reconstructed stage. Eastern cognates keep an affricate: Alabama and Koasati chinto, Creek cetto [tʃittoː], Mikasuki činti.
Compare Alabama and Koasati nochi, Creek nucetv [notʃita].
Compare Alabama and Koasati chakki, Creek cakketv.

Compare Alabama and Koasati nakchi. This is one of the isoglosses Haas (1941) used to separate Western Muskogean (Choctaw-Chickasaw) from the eastern languages; the proto-segment is written *c by Haas and *¢ [ts] by Booker.
Paunaka has no ts at all; *ts and *s merged as s in every context.
The change is documented between early 20th-century records and modern Terena, independently of Paunaka.
The Bata and Lamang groups instead have *ts → t (Proto-Bata fitɨ, Proto-Lamang fiti 'sun').

examples.note: Gravina treats the change as independent in Maltam, Mpade and Malgbe; in Malgbe it followed *s → j.
Saisiyat ⟨s⟩ is realized [s] or [θ]; Blust reconstructs *C as the affricate [ts].
